pedagogicalBasis: Context before production: short meaningful prompts anchor target grammar in a situation.
Controlled-to-freer progression: tasks ask learners to notice, complete, then personalise language.
No bulk filler: each task targets one unit objective and includes a model answer plus explanation.

tasks.objective: Use am/is/are to introduce people and give basic identity information.
tasks.prompt: Write three sentences about you and two people you know. Use am, is, and are once each.
tasks.modelAnswer: I am a student. My brother is at home. My friends are happy today.
tasks.explanation: The verb changes with the subject: I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are.

tasks.objective: Choose a, an, or the from first mention, vowel sound, and known object clues.
tasks.prompt: Complete the mini-dialogue: A: I want ___ apple and ___ sandwich. B: OK. Put ___ sandwich in this bag.
tasks.explanation: Use an before the vowel sound in apple, a before the consonant sound in sandwich, and the when the sandwich is now known.

tasks.objective: Describe simple places with in, on, and at using visible cues.
tasks.prompt: Look at your classroom. Write three true sentences with in, on, and at. Mention a real object or place.
tasks.modelAnswer: My book is on the desk. My pencils are in my bag. I am at my desk.
tasks.explanation: Use on for a surface, in for inside a container or place, and at for a point or position.

tasks.objective: Use am/is/are + -ing to describe actions happening now.
tasks.prompt: Imagine a family photo right now. Write four sentences: one with I am, one with he/she is, one with we are, and one with they are.
tasks.modelAnswer: I am smiling. My sister is reading. We are sitting in the kitchen. My parents are cooking dinner.
tasks.explanation: Present continuous needs the correct be verb plus an -ing verb for actions happening now.

tasks.objective: Choose will or going to for instant decisions, plans, and evidence-based predictions.
tasks.prompt: For each situation, write one sentence: 1) You see black clouds. 2) Your friend drops books. 3) You bought tickets for Friday.
tasks.modelAnswer: It is going to rain. I will help you. I am going to see a film on Friday.
tasks.explanation: Use going to when there is evidence or a plan; use will for an instant offer or decision.

tasks.objective: Use the first conditional to connect a realistic future condition with its result.
tasks.prompt: A classmate has an English exam tomorrow. Write three helpful first-conditional sentences for them.
tasks.modelAnswer: If you review the vocabulary tonight, you will remember more words. If you sleep early, you will feel fresh. If you panic, you will make small mistakes.
tasks.explanation: First conditional uses if + present simple for the condition and will + base verb for the future result.

tasks.objective: Use must, might, and can't to make deductions from evidence.
tasks.prompt: Read the clues and write one deduction for each: 1) The lights are on and music is playing. 2) I am not sure, but her bag is here. 3) Ali is in Izmir, so the person at the door is not Ali.
tasks.modelAnswer: They must be at home. She might be in the building. That can't be Ali at the door.
tasks.explanation: Use must for a strong positive deduction, might for uncertainty, and can't when the evidence makes something impossible.
